root_cause.text: In the s3c64xx SPI driver, the DMA-channel lifetime handling became inconsistent after DMA allocation was moved from probe() to s3c64xx_spi_prepare_transfer(), leaving s3c64xx_spi_remove() to unconditionally release sdd->rx_dma.ch and sdd->tx_dma.ch even when those channel pointers were never initialized.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that allocation was moved “from probe() back to s3c64xx_spi_prepare_transfer()” but the “corresponding deallocation” in remove() was not removed, and the patch fixes the NULL-deref by deleting the remove() calls to dma_release_channel(sdd->rx_dma.ch) and dma_release_channel(sdd->tx_dma.ch).

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop releasing SPI DMA channels during remove to avoid incorrect DMA cleanup in the s3c64xx SPI driver.
intent_record.what: The conditional block in s3c64xx_spi_remove() that checked !is_polling(sdd) and called dma_release_channel() for sdd->rx_dma.ch and sdd->tx_dma.ch was removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver no longer releases its RX and TX DMA channels during device removal in this function, avoiding those dma_release_channel() calls regardless of polling mode.

grouping_result.intent: Stop releasing SPI DMA channels during remove to avoid incorrect DMA cleanup in the s3c64xx SPI driver.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause: remove() was unconditionally releasing DMA channels that might never have been allocated after DMA setup moved out of probe(). Stopping DMA channel release during remove fixes that inconsistent lifetime handling.

candidates.rationale: This unconditionally releases the RX DMA channel during remove whenever polling is disabled, even though DMA channel allocation was moved out of probe and the channel pointer may never have been initialized.
This unconditionally releases the TX DMA channel during remove whenever polling is disabled, despite the channel possibly never having been allocated or initialized after the DMA lifetime change.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditionally releases the RX DMA channel in remove(), even after DMA allocation was moved to transfer preparation, so sdd->rx_dma.ch may be uninitialized or never allocated.
This unconditionally releases the TX DMA channel in remove(), despite the DMA channel lifetime change meaning sdd->tx_dma.ch may never have been initialized or allocated.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the DMA lifetime logic in prepare_transfer(), probe(), error paths, and remove(). The root cause describes a buggy state where DMA allocation was moved to s3c64xx_spi_prepare_transfer() while s3c64xx_spi_remove() still unconditionally released sdd->rx_dma.ch and sdd->tx_dma.ch even if never initialized. In this commit, that vulnerable pattern is not present. Instead, DMA acquisition is moved into probe(): `sdd->rx_dma.ch = dma_request_slave_channel_reason(&pdev->dev, "rx");` and `sdd->tx_dma.ch = dma_request_slave_channel_reason(&pdev->dev, "tx");`, both under `if (!is_polling(sdd))`. The old per-transfer request/release logic is removed from `s3c64xx_spi_prepare_transfer()` and `s3c64xx_spi_unprepare_transfer()` is deleted. The remove path releases channels only under the same condition: `if (!is_polling(sdd)) { dma_release_channel(sdd->rx_dma.ch); dma_release_channel(sdd->tx_dma.ch); }`, which matches the probe-time allocation model. Therefore the inconsistent lifetime handling described in the root cause is absent here, and this commit already contains the fix by keeping DMA channel allocation in probe() and release in remove().

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the DMA-channel lifetime change directly in the relevant functions. The vulnerable root cause described is: DMA allocation moved out of probe() into prepare_transfer(), while remove() still unconditionally released sdd->rx_dma.ch and sdd->tx_dma.ch even if never initialized. In this commit, that vulnerable state is not present. Instead, DMA allocation is moved into probe(): `sdd->rx_dma.ch = dma_request_slave_channel_reason(&pdev->dev, "rx");` and `sdd->tx_dma.ch = dma_request_slave_channel_reason(&pdev->dev, "tx");`, both under `if (!is_polling(sdd))`. The old per-transfer allocation in `s3c64xx_spi_prepare_transfer()` is removed, leaving only `spi->dma_rx = sdd->rx_dma.ch;` and `spi->dma_tx = sdd->tx_dma.ch;`. Also, per-transfer release is removed entirely by deleting `s3c64xx_spi_unprepare_transfer()` and clearing `master->unprepare_transfer_hardware`. Finally, `s3c64xx_spi_remove()` releases DMA only in the same `if (!is_polling(sdd))` mode where probe acquired them: `dma_release_channel(sdd->rx_dma.ch); dma_release_channel(sdd->tx_dma.ch);`. Therefore the inconsistent lifetime pattern from the root cause is absent here, and this commit already contains the fix by keeping DMA request/release in probe/remove instead of prepare/remove.
